data.title: Racing Force: Buy Rating Reiterated on Strong Motorsport Momentum, Diversification Progress and Unchanged $6 Price Target
data.description:
Racing Force SpA, the Consumer Cyclical sector company, was revisited by a Wall Street analyst today. Analyst from Equita Sim maintained a Buy rating on the stock and has a €6.00 price target.

analyst has given his Buy rating due to a combination of factors, chiefly the robust momentum in the global motorsport market and Racing Force’s strengthened competitive positioning. Management meetings confirmed solid growth prospects for 2026–2027, supported by structural expansion in the U.S., where market size matches EMEA but current revenue contribution remains materially lower.

The analyst also highlights progressing diversification initiatives such as Milipol, ZN Comm, and Driver’s Eye, which are approaching more meaningful monetization and could add new revenue streams. Operational resilience, evidenced by the uninterrupted helmet production in Bahrain despite geopolitical tensions, further underpins confidence, and the unchanged price target of $6 reflects attractive upside versus the current share price.

data.title: Analyst Reaffirms Buy on Sabaf as Global Demand Bottoms, Setting €16 Target Price for Upside on Margin Recovery and Operating Leverage
data.description:
In a report released today, from Equita Sim maintained a Buy rating on Sabaf Technology and Safety, with a price target of €16.00.

analyst has given his Buy rating due to a combination of factors, primarily the company’s ability to resume revenue growth in a weak market and the visibility provided by solid orders and strategic expansions in India and Mexico. Despite some pressure on margins from input cost inflation and FX, Sabaf is managing profitability and implementing price increases, which should support earnings as these initiatives fully materialize.

At the current share price, valuation multiples are low relative to the group’s earnings and cash generation potential, especially considering demand is still at the bottom of the cycle in key regions. The updated target price of €16 per share, based on DCF and peer multiples, implies meaningful upside and reflects confidence that Sabaf’s strengthened industrial footprint will deliver operating leverage and margin recovery once market conditions normalize.

data.title: Wickes: Buy Rating Backed by Resilient H1, Strengthening Q3 Momentum and Attractive Sub‑10x Valuation
data.description:
Andrew Wade, an analyst from Jefferies, maintained the Buy rating on Wickes Group. The associated price target is p250.00.

Andrew Wade has given his Buy rating due to a combination of factors, including Wickes’ resilient first-half performance and clear operational progress. Profit before tax in H1 FY26 edged higher versus last year as revenue growth and cost efficiencies offset inflation, while strategic initiatives such as TradePro expansion, market share gains, and new store openings are strengthening the business model.

Crucially, trading momentum has improved meaningfully in Q3, with like-for-like retail sales moving into mid‑single‑digit growth, supporting management’s confidence in meeting full‑year profit expectations. Against a backdrop of market worries about potential estimate cuts and given the shares’ valuation at below 10x earnings, Wade views Wickes as offering an attractive risk‑reward profile, underpinned by a differentiated customer proposition and robust double‑digit profit delivery over time.
